name: Nigeria
genZNote: Nigeria is Africa's most populous country AND its largest economy — and 'Nollywood', its film industry, actually produces more movies per year than Hollywood, which surprises almost everyone the first time they hear it.

sections.heading: 🗺️ Geography
bullets: Located in West Africa on the Gulf of Guinea, bordered by Benin, Niger, Chad, and Cameroon.
Diverse terrain ranging from coastal mangrove swamps and tropical rainforest in the south to savanna in the north, with the Niger and Benue Rivers as major waterways.
Africa's most populous country, with over 200 million people and more than 250 distinct ethnic groups.

sections.heading: 🗣️ People & Culture
bullets: English is the official language, alongside major indigenous languages including Hausa, Yoruba, and Igbo, reflecting its ethnic diversity.
Roughly evenly split between a Muslim-majority north and a Christian-majority south, a divide that significantly shapes national politics.
Home to Nollywood, one of the world's largest film industries by volume of output, and a globally influential Afrobeats music scene.

sections.heading: 🏛️ Government & Society
bullets: A federal presidential republic composed of 36 states and a Federal Capital Territory (Abuja), modelled partly on the US federal system.
Gained independence from British colonial rule in 1960, and experienced periods of military rule interspersed with democratic governance through much of its post-independence history.
Returned to sustained civilian democratic rule in 1999 after decades of intermittent military governments.

sections.heading: 🧬 Medical & Scientific Developments
bullets: Africa's largest economy and a growing hub for technology startups ('Silicon Lagoon' in Lagos), particularly in fintech.
Significant public health challenges and successes, including its declaration as free of wild poliovirus by the WHO in 2020, a major public health milestone.
Growing pharmaceutical manufacturing capacity aimed at reducing reliance on imported medicines across West Africa.

sections.heading: 🌐 Global Relations
bullets: Africa's largest economy by GDP and most populous nation, giving it significant regional and continental influence.
A founding member of the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) and an influential voice in African Union affairs.
A major contributor to UN peacekeeping missions and regional security efforts, including combating the Boko Haram insurgency in its northeast.

sections.heading: 🇮🇳 Relations with India
bullets: India and Nigeria maintain a 'Strategic Partnership', with Nigeria being one of India's largest trading partners in Africa, particularly for crude oil imports.
A significant Indian business community has operated in Nigeria for decades, especially in manufacturing, pharmaceuticals, and textiles.
India has extended lines of credit and development assistance to Nigeria across infrastructure, healthcare, and agriculture sectors.

sections.heading: 📦 Trade & Economy
bullets: Africa's largest economy, historically dependent on oil and gas exports, though increasingly diversifying into technology, agriculture, and entertainment (Nollywood, Afrobeats).
A major global crude oil producer and OPEC member, though facing challenges from oil theft, pipeline vandalism, and the need for economic diversification.
A rapidly growing fintech and startup ecosystem, attracting significant international venture capital investment.

sections.heading: ⭐ What It's Known For
bullets: Being Africa's most populous nation and largest economy.
Nollywood, one of the world's largest film industries by output.
Afrobeats music's major global cultural influence.
Being a major OPEC oil producer and growing African tech/fintech hub.

sections.heading: 💰 Currency & Economy
bullets: Currency: Nigerian Naira (NGN).
Africa's most populous country and one of its largest economies, heavily reliant on oil exports alongside a rapidly growing technology and entertainment sector (Nollywood, fintech).

sections.heading: 🌿 Ecology & Environment
bullets: Ecosystems range from Niger Delta mangroves and rainforest in the south to savanna in the north.
The Niger Delta faces significant environmental challenges linked to oil extraction.

sections.heading: 📜 History & Major Turning Points
bullets: Home to historic kingdoms and empires, including the Benin Empire and the Sokoto Caliphate.
Became a British colony/protectorate before gaining independence in 1960.
Endured a civil war (the Biafran War, 1967-1970) shortly after independence.

sections.heading: 🏛️ Major Political & Constitutional Changes
bullets: 1960 independence from Britain; became a republic in 1963.
Experienced repeated military coups before transitioning to sustained civilian democratic rule in 1999 under the Fourth Republic.

sections.heading: 🏅 Sports, Arts & Global Recognition
bullets: Football is the most popular sport; the national team has won multiple Africa Cup of Nations titles.
Nollywood is one of the world's largest film industries by output.
Afrobeats music, pioneered by artists like Fela Kuti, has major global cultural influence.

sections.heading: 🌐 International Organizations & Important Memberships
bullets: Founding member of the African Union and ECOWAS (Economic Community of West African States).
Member of the UN and the Commonwealth of Nations; a significant contributor to UN and regional peacekeeping.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: Nigeria is Africa's most populous country and largest economy, a federal presidential republic in West Africa known for oil production, Nollywood, and Afrobeats music.
keyFacts: Capital: Abuja (largest city: Lagos). Currency: Nigerian Naira.
Federal presidential republic; 36 states plus the Federal Capital Territory.
Africa's most populous nation and largest economy by GDP.
Major OPEC oil producer; home to Nollywood, a top global film industry by output.
commonConfusion: Nigeria's capital is Abuja, not Lagos — Lagos is the largest city and commercial capital, but Abuja became the official capital in 1991.

highYieldFacts: Nigeria: federal presidential republic; capital Abuja; Africa's most populous nation and largest economy.
Major OPEC oil producer; home to Nollywood (top film industry by output) and Afrobeats music.
India-Nigeria: Strategic Partnership; major crude oil trade partner for India in Africa.
commonTraps: Assuming Lagos is Nigeria's capital — it is Abuja, since 1991.
Assuming Nigeria is religiously/ethnically homogeneous — it has a roughly even Muslim-north/Christian-south split and 250+ ethnic groups.
mustRemember: Nigeria: Africa's largest economy/population, capital Abuja, OPEC member, Nollywood/Afrobeats cultural powerhouse, key India oil partner.
